answer.rationale: Rollback is blocked by compliance due to the security patch. Regional failover (memory_b2) risks dropping or duplicating in-flight writes during cutover, which conflicts with the explicit objective of not losing customer writes, especially under heavy settlement load. Add_capacity (memory_b3) was validated as a preemptive measure before a known surge, not as a reactive fix for an active 90-minute degradation, so its latency-to-effect is uncertain. Enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) addressed a dependency outage, not a primary-region resource contention pattern, so it doesn't match this failure mode. Memory_b5 describes the closest analog: report/read query load on the primary contending with transactional writes, resolved by routing reads to replicas with same-day recovery in write latency, without touching the write path itself. This directly targets the observed symptom (write-path p99 degradation confined to primary) with minimal risk to write durability. I want to verify memory_b5's archived record before committing, since it is the sole basis for believing this action addresses a write-latency problem via a read-side change, and I want to confirm the original conditions (e.g., whether primary contention was confirmed to be read-driven) match this incident's likely cause before spending the one available intervention.
